title: Few-Body Decay Dynamics in Colloidal CsPbI3 Quantum-Dot Clusters
authors: Emma Daggett, Christian M. Lange, Nicholas Favate, Ankit Kundu, Ishita Agarwal, Arya D. Keni, Adhyyan S. Mansukhani, Christina W. Li, Libai Huang, Jonathan D. Hood
abstract: Colloidal perovskite quantum dots combine bright emission with the ability to self- assemble into closely spaced structures, enabling radiative dynamics to be studied from isolated emitters to few-dot clusters. Here, we characterize CsPbI3 perovskite quan- tum dots from isolated emitters to self-assembled clusters containing up to ten dots. We estimate the number of emitters in each cluster using a combination of photon autocorrelation, blinking statistics, and emission brightness. Compared with isolated dots, clusters containing two or more emitters exhibit biexponential decay, with a short lifetime that decreases with emitter number and an additional long-lived component. Photon-correlation Fourier spectroscopy shows that the single-dot emission remains far from the lifetime-limited regime. Nevertheless, we observe emitter-number-dependent decay dynamics even in this low-coherence regime. Together, these measurements es- tablish self-assembled perovskite quantum-dot clusters as a platform for studying how collective optical behavior emerges between the single-emitter and ensemble limits
summary: The authors investigated how the optical decay dynamics of CsPbI3 quantum dots change as they self-assemble into clusters. By measuring photon correlations and decay lifetimes, they found that clusters exhibit a biexponential decay profile, confirming the emergence of collective optical behavior. This work establishes the quantum-dot cluster as a platform to study the transition from single-emitter to ensemble quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study characterizes the collective optical behavior and radiative decay dynamics of colloidal CsPbI3 quantum-dot clusters, bridging the gap between isolated emitters and ensemble limits.
main_result: The decay dynamics transition from single-exponential (isolated dots) to biexponential (clusters $\ge 2$), indicating collective decay mechanisms are active even in the low-coherence regime.
method: The research employs photon autocorrelation, blinking statistics, and Photon-correlation Fourier spectroscopy (PCFS) to measure decay rates and coherence times.
model_or_system: The physical system is colloidal CsPbI3 perovskite quantum dots, studied from single emitters up to clusters of ten dots. The analysis compares measured decay traces to theoretical models of coupled two-level emitters.
key_observables: Biexponential decay components ($	au_{	ext{short}}, 	au_{	ext{long}}$), photon-correlation function $g^{(2)}(	au)$, and coherence time $T_2$.
important_parameters: Cluster size ($N=1$ to $N=10$), decay rates ($\Gamma_B, \Gamma_D$), and the ratio of fast-to-slow decay components ($\sim 1/N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares measurements to idealized models (e.g., independent excitation vs. coherent coupling) and notes that the long-lived component mechanism remains ambiguous.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate TEM images, $g^{(2)}(	au)$ measurements confirming antibunching, and decay traces showing the transition from single to biexponential decay as the cluster size increases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the system using multiple diagnostics (photon statistics, coherence) before modeling the decay dynamics by comparing measurements against theoretical limits for single-emitter, two-emitter, and larger cluster behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental evidence of collective quantum optical behavior in solid-state nanocrystal ensembles, directly addressing how inter-particle coupling modifies fundamental decay processes, which is highly relevant to quantum light sources and cavity QED.
